result.summary: This is a life-safety emergency. At 23:41 the tenant reported a gas smell and the carbon monoxide alarm going off, with a toddler in the flat. I texted the tenant immediate steps: get everyone out, call the National Gas Emergency Service, and call 999 if anyone has symptoms. I also assigned the landlord's preferred gas engineer, Calder Heating, without waiting for landlord approval, emailed them and texted the landlord. I escalated to the on-call team at high priority, because the urgent next steps are phone calls my tools can't make. Those calls are to the tenant, Calder's emergency line and the landlord's out-of-hours number.
result.situation: Overnight report from the tenant of Flat 2, 5 Linden Terrace, Harrowby ZZ7 3ZZ: a gas smell in the kitchen and the CO alarm sounding, with a toddler asleep upstairs (event 001). The CRM note (event 002) says the landlord, Ms R. Aziz, usually doesn't answer overnight but has an out-of-hours number on file. The preferred gas engineer is Calder Heating: their office closes at 17:30, but they have an emergency line.

The emergency rule lets us dispatch work without landlord approval. A human is needed because the next steps are live phone calls overnight.
